newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's Zedillo denies he is a weak leader.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's Zedillo denies he is a weak leader.

text.p: Mexico's President Ernesto Zedillo on Wednesday dismissed charges that he was a weak leader and told Mexicans that he had no magic wand to speed up economic recovery following last year's crushing recession.

Zedillo, in an interview with Spanish-language TV channel Univision, also gave the cold shoulder to his disgraced predecessor Carlos Salinas de Gortari and revealed that he had received threats associated with the slaying of Luis Donaldo Colosio, the original ruling party choice for the presidency.
Asked if he was a weak president, as many Mexicans view him, Zedillo dismissed such opinions as "subjective" and said he was in full control of the government.
"I have to act with full responsibility and with complete realism," he added. "It would be no use, and what's more it would be lying to people, to say: 'We will solve your problems by magic'."
A transcript of the interview was released by Zedillo's office.

Zedillo said he was never a friend of Salinas, who left the country in disgrace in March last year following his brother's arrest on murder charges and government charges that he was responsible for the December 1994 peso crash.

"I was a servant of Carlos Salinas de Gortari in his capacity as President of the Republic," Zedillo said. "I do not think I had a relationship that could be characterised as one of friendship, not before and not during his term."

Zedillo said he had last spoken to Salinas on December 1, 1994 -- the day he assumed the presidency -- and knew only from newspaper reports that Salinas was in Ireland. He denied allegations that he cut a deal with the former president to ensure his silence in self-imposed exile.

"There has been no agreement with him, nor with any former Mexican president, on any matter," he said, denying reports that he had secretly met Salinas in March 1995 shortly before he left the country.

Asked what he knew about the March 23, 1994 assassination of Colosio, for whom Zedillo was campaign manager, the Mexican President denied having anything to do with security arrangements for the slain candidate.
Investigators believe the killing was a conspiracy involving members of Colosio's security team, but have been unable to prove their theory.
"I did not know about security arrangements. The campaign manager only coordinated strategy, other people were in charge of security arrangements," he said.
"Something very interesting is that when I was candidate for the presidency, some threats were made against me, linked to the tragic death of Luis Donaldo," he said. He gave no other details.
